'''Ingrid del Carmen Montes González''' (born 1958), is a Puerto Rican chemist who is a professor in at the [[University of Puerto Rico, Río Piedras Campus]]. Her research focus is on [[Chemistry education|chemical education]] and [[organometallic chemistry]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ingridmontes.org/home/research/|title=Research|website=IngridMontes.org|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-17}}</ref>  Montes has been Director-at-large at the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS) since 2013.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/elections/directorlarge-Ingrid-Montes/96/i36|title=For director-at-large: Ingrid Montes|journal=Chemical & Engineering News |volume=96 |issue=36}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i36/DirectorLarge-Ingrid-Montes.html|title=For Director-At-Large: Ingrid Montes |journal=Chemical & Engineering News |volume=93 |issue=36}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i37/DirectorLarge-Ingrid-Montes.html|title=For Director-At-Large: Ingrid Montes |journal=Chemical & Engineering News |volume=93 |issue=37}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/about/governance/elections.html|title=Elections|website=American Chemical Society|language=en|access-date=2019-02-23}}</ref> Montes founded the "Festival de Química" (Chemistry Festival) in 2005, this program was then adopted by the ACS in 2010.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/global/international/regional/eventsglobal/festivaldequimica.html|title=ACS Festival de Química|website=American Chemical Society|language=en|access-date=2019-02-23}}</ref>

== Education ==
Montes attended the [[University of Puerto Rico, Río Piedras Campus]] (UPR-RP).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Dr. Montes CV |url=http://www.ingridmontes.org/home/drmontescv/ |access-date=2019-06-17 |website=IngridMontes.org |language=en-US}}</ref> She earned a B.S. in chemistry in 1980 and went on to complete a Ph.D. in [[organic chemistry]] in 1985 under the supervision of Gerald Larson.<ref name=":1" /> Her doctoral research focused on [[organometallic chemistry]], particularly the synthesis of functionalized [[organosilanes]] and their applications in [[organic synthesis]].<ref name=":1" />

Montes began became a teaching assistant at UPR-RP in 1980.<ref name=":1" /> From 1981 to 1984, she worked as a research assistant while pursuing her doctoral studies, contributing to laboratory research in organometallic chemistry.<ref name=":1" /> In 1984, Montes also served as a part-time instructor at [[Interamerican University of Puerto Rico]], teaching general and organic chemistry.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Montes was a lecturer at the College of Pharmacy at [[University of Puerto Rico, Medical Sciences Campus]] from 1985 to 1986 and as a curriculum specialist at Puerto Rico Junior College from 1986 to 1988.<ref name=":1" /> In 1987, she joined the faculty at UPR-RP as an assistant professor in the department of chemistry, where she taught courses in general chemistry, organic chemistry, organic synthesis, and [[hazardous waste]] disposal.<ref name=":1" /> Her research at the time focused on the synthesis of [[ferrocene]] derivatives, exploring their potential applications in [[catalysis]], sensors, and [[materials science]].<ref name=":1" /> She developed a strong interest in [[Chemistry education|chemical education]], emphasizing the use of inquiry-based and active learning approaches in teaching organic chemistry.<ref name=":1" />

Montes was promoted to associate professor in 1992 and became a full professor in 1998.<ref name=":1" /> During this period, her research interests expanded to include the synthesis and characterization of ferrocenyl chalcones and their potential applications in biological systems, polymers, and sensors.<ref name=":1" /> Her work contributed to understanding the redox properties of ferrocene derivatives and their use in [[Electrochemistry|electrochemical]] sensors.<ref name=":1" /> She also played a role in chemical education, integrating active learning strategies and developing laboratory manuals for organic chemistry courses.<ref name=":1" /> Her work on chemical education included studies on different learning styles and their impact on student achievement in organic chemistry.<ref name=":1" /> Montes co-authored several laboratory manuals used in chemistry education at UPR.<ref name=":1" /> Montes served as coordinator of the Pre-MARC Program (a training program for minority students in biomedical research) from 1995 and assistant to the chairman in academic affairs from 1996 to 1998.<ref name=":1" /> In 2015, she was appointed assistant dean of graduate studies and research at UPR-RP.<ref name=":1" />

Montes founded the “Festival de Química” in 2005, a community outreach event designed to demonstrate the importance of chemistry in everyday life.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-06-16 |title=Sobre el Festival de la Química |url=https://www.cienciapr.org/en/node/12259 |access-date=2019-02-23 |website=Ciencia Puerto Rico |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> The initiative, initially implemented in Puerto Rico, expanded internationally through the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS).<ref name=":1" /> Her involvement with ACS extended beyond outreach; she held leadership positions, including chair of the committee on community activities.<ref name=":1" /> She also served as president of the Puerto Rico section of ACS, contributing to the development of educational resources and mentoring programs for chemistry students.<ref name=":1" /> Montes is a fellow of ACS.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Ainsworth |first=Susan J. |date=January 30, 2012 |title=Award for Volunteer Service to the American Chemical Society |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i5/Award-Volunteer-Service-American-Chemical.html |journal=Chemical & Engineering News |volume=90 |issue=5 |issn=0009-2347}}</ref> In 2012, she was awarded the ACS volunteer service award.<ref name=":3" />

In 2017, she received the Distinguished Women in Chemistry or Chemical Engineering Award from the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-03-07 |title=Awardees of the IUPAC 2017 Distinguished Women in Chemistry or Chemical Engineering |url=https://iupac.org/iupac-2017-distinguished-women/ |access-date=2019-02-23 |website=IUPAC {{!}} International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry |language=en-US}}</ref> The following year, she was recognized as with the Mujer Puertorriqueña Distinguida en STEM, G Works, Inc.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-03-07 |title=Boricuas exitosas en carreras STEM |url=https://www.primerahora.com/estilos-de-vida/mujer/nota/boricuasexitosasencarrerasstem-1210422/ |access-date=2019-02-23 |website=Primera Hora |language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, Montes was awarded the Dr. Osvaldo Ramírez Torres Award, the highest honor of the Chemists Association of Puerto Rico.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premios |url=https://cqpr1941.com/galeria-y-premios/ |access-date=11 February 2026 |website=Colegio de Químicos de Puerto Rico}}</ref>
